articleTitle: Improving the Performance of Bully Algorithm for Leader Election in Distributed Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Leader election is a classical problem in distributed systems in which the selection a coordinator node to perform tasks is necessary. However, coordinator can fail and this requires performing a leader election operation to choose a new coordinator. This study focuses on the Bully algorithm which uses a lot of messages and higher network traffic which are considered the main drawback. This paper provides a simple and adaptable adaptive bully algorithm that lowers the messages passing used and is simple and flexible. The algorithm utilizes only one node, called responsibility for the election, and a time span, where a time span is set for each node. These two procedures minimize leader election operations especially discovering failures from multiple processes in the system and messages passing. According to the results, the enhanced algorithm is better than the algorithm bully. It reduces the complexity of message passing during leader election operations.

articleTitle: Quantum Internet: Functionalities, Protocols and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In the recent years, and with the rapid development in the field of Quantum Internet (QI) and its applications, and as a result of this development, researchers showed the difference between the traditional internet and the QI. The present study discusses more about the concept of the QI, especially the functionalities, protocols, and applications of QI. This study gives researchers and readers a deeper knowledge about the QI in general and its applications in particular, and how these applications have helped the QI to be better than the current internet in the coming years through more secure and provide a high and optimizations of performance, more reliability, high speed when implementing, and fewer errors.

articleTitle: Enhancing a Random Forest Model Based on Single Rule Reduction for Tax Evasion Depends on the Values of K in K-Fold Validation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: This paper developed a new model called Single Rule Random Forest (SrRF) that enhances the performance of the Fandom Forest technique(RF)and reduces its rules, then compared the performance of this model with a set of ML models as follows (DT, RF, GPT) of the datasets provided by the Tax Authority of Yemen which consists of 1083 records using two values for k in K-Fold Cross Validation). The results showed that by using the value k=10, the GPT Classifier gave the highest result of 100 % but this result will cause overfitting, then the SRI-RF Classifier gave the best result with 99.89%, while RF gave the worst result. By using the value k=5, the GPT Classifier also gave the highest result of 100 % but this result also caused overfitting, then the SrRF Classifier gave the best result, while RF gave the worst result. From the above, the researchers also note that training the data using K-fold cross-validation with the value K=10 gave better results. On the other side, our proposed model SRIRF with the value of k=10 gave the best result.

articleTitle: Yoga Pose Estimation using PoseNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)

authors.preferredName: Kolaparthi Venkata Satya Naga Sai Kishan

abstract: Yoga has become an integral part of exercise practice in the holistic health regimen, greatly impacting on the physical, mental, and emotional well-being. It enhances flexibility, strength, and balance while promoting relaxation and stress reduction. To reap these benefits without causing harm, it is essential to perform yoga poses correctly. A reliable estimator of the pose is needed to maintain proper alignment and gain the maximum from each session. The proposed model integrated with CNN, helps users achieve correct postures by pausing the session timer until the user successfully maintains the correct alignment. This ensures that the user remains focused on achieving proper posture before moving to the next asana. The proposed approach supports users in improving their yoga practicing techniques by ensuring that progression can be done when optimal posture is maintained, encouraging a safe and effective yoga practice that aligns with personal health goals.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Efficiency in UAV Cognitive Radio Networks: A Machine Learning-Based Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle has gained much popularity in these years due to the broad utilization in performing various tasks that range from monitoring, collecting data, and surveillance. However, all these are limited by the battery life of UAVs, which further determines the fly distance and time. Different methods have, therefore, been suggested for the optimization of energy for UAVs. One approach that can be employed to enable energy efficiency in UAVs with dynamic access to available spectrum resources is by considering cognitive radio networks. This article presents the study of UAVs cognitive radio networks for energy efficiency optimization. Since UAVs can offer effective and flexible communication services, their usage in cognitive radio networks has attracted a lot of attention. However, owing to the limited energy resources of UAVs, dependable and sustainable communication is difficult to achieve. This work may provide great insight into the design and optimization of UAV-based cognitive radio networks toward reliable and sustainable communication services. In this paper, we present an energy-efficient optimization strategy taking into consideration the network dynamic structure and different energy usages for the UAVs. The following is proposed in this paper as an algorithm that uses ML techniques for the estimation of energy consumption for UAVs, which then tunes the adjustment of the routing pathways. Simulation results show that the proposed method enhances energy efficiency with constant network performance.

articleTitle: Optimizing YOLOv8-cls: A Step Towards Smarter Edge Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Optimized YOLOv8 for classifying images into predefined labels is proposed to efficiently deploy convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on Internet of Things (IoT) edge devices. It is an advanced deep learning (DL) model with limited memory and rapid inference requirements. This research improves the YOLOv8 model architecture for classifying tasks by incorporating Dynamic Range Quantization (DRQ), which enhanced the YOLOv8n-cls model by reducing the model size by 75% while achieving an accuracy of 90.4% and 91.8% on datasets related to identifying Leaf illness and Waste classification datasets, respectively. Comparison with previous studies demonstrates that this proposed model offers model sizes and faster inference times while maintaining accuracy, making it well-suited for edge environments with limited memory capacity.

articleTitle: Embedding Virtual and Augmented Reality in Higher Education in Yemeni Universities
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) have increasingly applied to different areas including medicine, engineering, advertising, tourism, entertainment, training, and education. Although VR and AR are still new and not yet used in higher education in Yemen, many colleges and universities worldwide have implemented multimedia and VR/AR technologies as promising learning tools. VR/AR technologies effectively add more engagement, motivation, retention, satisfaction, and enjoyment into learning process when compared to the traditional teaching and learning methods. The aim of the paper is to highlight the uses of VR and AR in different scenarios in many areas and more specifically in higher education and distance learning. In this paper, simple models are proposed and presented to help universities and policymakers in Yemen adopt these innovative technologies and encourage them to invest more resources and training towards implementing those technologies within their curriculum.

articleTitle: Optimizing Computation Offloading in UAV-Enhanced Mobile Edge Computing through a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Method
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In this study, we explore the concept of drone-assisted drones. In a mobile edge computing (MEC) setting, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) play a critical role in providing offloading services to mobile devices in regions lacking adequate infrastructure, UAVs are utilized for delivering offloading services to nearby mobile devices (UEs), with the primary objective being the minimization of processing delays under constraints involving discrete variables. by collectively enhancing user scheduling, balancing task offloading, adjusting UAV flight angles, and optimizing flight speeds, we aim to enhance the efficiency and performance of the system. Given the non-convex nature of the issue, the extensive range of states, and the continuous actions involved, this paper proposes. A computational strategy for offloading that employs the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) technique. within the domain of Reinforcement Learning (RL). The results from the experiments clearly show the effectiveness of the suggested algorithm. converges toward the optimal solution, markedly enhancing processing speeds and system performance. This study sheds light on the remarkable advancements achieved through our proposed solution, showing tangible improvements in processing efficiency and system efficacy.

Author Keywords: deep deterministic policy gradient. Computation offloading

articleTitle: Real-Time Intrusion Detection and Traffic Analysis Using AI Techniques in IoT Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In light of the growing number of cyberattacks and the rapid boom in network traffic, it's crucial to discover network traffic anomalies or intrusions as they occur. Manual inspection is inefficient due to the massive volume, velocity, and variety of network traffic data. This research aims to broaden a clever, real-time anomaly detection framework using deep learning to know strategies within big statistics environments. The proposed technique makes use of multilayer feedforward neural networks, evaluated on benchmark intrusion datasets and large-scale actual network traffic, to pick out relevant traffic functions. This paper carries lengthy-short-term memory (LSTM) models and convolutional neural networks (CNN) based on packet seize facts. The model's overall performance is evaluated by the use of the G-Mean metric, which assesses the balance between sensitivity and specificity. The G-Mean is specifically beneficial in coping with imbalanced datasets through comparing the model's performance throughout both tremendous and terrible classes. The deep learning models demonstrated advanced anomaly detection talents as compared to conventional shallow gaining knowledge of strategies. This comprehensive method highlights the ability of deep learning for real-time anomaly detection, substantially improving network protection within huge statistics environments, including the Internet of Things (IoT).

articleTitle: Orderlikey: Smart Kiosk Ordering System for F&B Sustainable Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Orderlikey is an innovative web-kiosk system specifically designed for implementation at FK kiosks, with a primary focus on minimizing errors and reducing processing times. By offering real-time data on menu options and kiosk status, Orderlikey achieves its core goal of streamlining operations and reducing inefficiencies. Building on existing technological advancements in the F&B sector, this study uniquely addresses the specific challenges faced by FK Kiosks through the development of Orderlikey. This system uniquely integrates Self-Order System (SOS), Point of Sale (POS), and Kitchen Display System (KDS) technologies, tailored for a university kiosk environment—a combination not previously explored. Utilizing the Rapid Application Development (RAD) methodology, the project progressed through module identification, the creation of a mobile-web adjunct application, and thorough user acceptance testing (UAT), ensuring adaptability and continuous improvement. The implementation of Orderlikey is expected to significantly enhance the efficiency of kiosk operations at FK, promising improved user satisfaction and contributing to a sustainable and transformed user environment through its user-centered, innovative approach.

articleTitle: WAEI: An Intelligent Chatbot for Helping Fighting the Pandemic Infodemic
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) began warning of a possible upcoming epidemic called monkeypox, while humanity is still suffering from the consequences of the latest epidemic. In addition to various health issues caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, an "infodemic" accompanied the virus that led to the spread of many fake news about the virus and possible medication treatments. This fake news led to the emergence of huge mass panic causing stress and anxiety and might lead to death. This paper proposes an intelligent Chatbot called WAEI (Arabic term means awareness in English) to increase the awareness of pandemic risks, methods of prevention, and precautionary measures. WAEI fight the infodemic by producing responses based on its knowledgebase that was formed from credible sources, namely the WHO. The Chatbot uses Natural Language Understanding (NLU) to infer its responses. 308 volunteers evaluated the proposed chatbot. The volunteers’ responses were statistically analyzed to measure whether the Chatbot is resourceful, coherent, and achieves user satisfaction. Precision, recall and F1 metrics shows improvement in accuracy, which reach 83% accuracy in responding to users’ inquiry. WAEI is of great value and has been proposed at the right time for the health sectors as it gives a good experience in using technology and smart systems to quickly handle infodemic effectively by providing necessary awareness for any potential foreseen diseases.

articleTitle: Hybrid Graphical Password Authentication Technique Based On GLCM And Canny Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The process of verifying the identity of someone requesting access to a computer system, network, or piece of hardware is known as authentication. One of the most popular forms of authentication is the usage of alphanumeric passwords. Because human memory is limited, things can be forgotten. Moreover, password-recovery software can crack text-based passwords. An alternate kind of password authentication that uses visuals rather than text is called a graphic password. This paper aims to create an automatic click-point graphical password system based on hybrid techniques that offer quick processing times, large password space with high-security levels, and low storage requirements. The suggested method is predicated on GLCM texture features (homogeneity and entropy), and canny edge detection. Additionally, the creation of an Android application based on the AES method with a password recovery problem to carry out the suggested job at an allowed level. Several devices are used to test and evaluate the application. Every strategy performs admirably in terms of point generation processing time. Compared to the prior graphical password method, the new approach enhances password strength in terms of password space. Regarding the randomization test, all protocols demonstrated excellent performance and passed all applicable tests. That shows a large password space of about with large entropy and a fast login time of about (6 s).

articleTitle: Optimizing Latency for Augmented Reality Applications via Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: One of the most prominent forms of technological integration is that between Augmented Reality (AR) and Cloud Computing, which provides significant storage and processing capabilities, breaking the limitations of relying on the computational power of the end-user devices. Enabling real-time interaction between users and virtual objects, which is provided in AR by blending virtual elements with the user's real environment, that requires high-speed data transmission and real-time responsiveness, as any noticeable delay can disrupt the user’s immersive experience. However, the issue of increased latency emerged as a critical challenge, which is particularly problematic for AR applications due to their need for low latency and high responsiveness to ensure an optimal user experience. This paper demonstrates the crucial role of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC)—located closer to the users—as a component of cloud computing in mitigating the high latency challenges. Furthermore, the paper highlights the significant impact of MEC, particularly in regions with emerging infrastructure, through practical experiments. Based on the results of these experiments, the paper emphasizes the need to expand the adoption of MEC to create high-quality AR experiences.

articleTitle: Knowledge Transfer Challenges: A Practical Study of Yemen Public Telecommunication Corporation
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The success of organizations today relies heavily on their intellectual capital, as knowledge is a key resource for value creation. Sharing and transferring knowledge enhances its value, embedding it within an organization’s processes and boosting competitiveness. This study focuses on the Yemen public telecommunication corporation (YPTC), which has adopted a knowledge-focused management approach. This study aims to explore challenges related to knowledge transfer in Yemen’s public sector, where such research is lacking. Using a descriptive and analytical method, data were collected via a questionnaire from 200 employees, yielding a response rate of 88%. The findings indicate a high level of knowledge transfer at YPTC, with individual, organizational, and technological factors identified as significant influences. The key barriers include trust, information technology support, motivation, and social networks.

articleTitle: E-Assessment of Question-Answering Scoring Using Semantic Text Matching In Arabic Language
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Smart technologies are vital for progressions in text processing. They support the enhancement of academic activities' efficiency. For e-assessment, they provide researchers and educators with tools for objective content evaluation and scoring. As demand for quality learning experiences increases, such technologies offer solutions to enrich education and expand understanding of course materials. Automated question-answering scoring (QAS) addresses the challenges of manual grading, which is labor-intensive and prone to mistakes. By integrating computer systems with natural language processing (NLP) and intelligent algorithms, student answers can be analyzed objectively, delivering accurate feedback to help improve skills. In this study, we have employed WordNet and TF-IDF for QAS tasks, based on text similarity matching methods. Text pre-processing techniques are utilized for reliable computational analysis of the Arabic language. This study combines two established methods in linguistic computing and text processing to automate the assessment of the question-answering method. Using a dataset of questions, teachers' templates, and students' answers. The results exhibited the distinction of WordNet over TF-IDF based on three evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: A review of Intrusion Detection Systems for the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Over the years, the Internet of Things has brought significant benefits to modern society, lives, and industries; however, the technology used has yet to mature sufficiently to provide secure devices and communication. Recently, the number of connected devices rapidly grows, thus adversaries have more opportunities to gain access to IoT devices and use them to launch what is called large-scale attacks. With the rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, the need for efficient and effective Intrusion Detection System (IDS) tailored for IoT environments has become increasingly paramount. This paper explores various techniques employed in contemporary IoT IDS, including traditional signature-based approaches like Snort and Bro/Zeek, as well as emerging deep learning-based methods.

articleTitle: Efficient Deployment of Nodes in a WSN Using a Modified PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are of great importance in various military and civilian applications, such as data collection and area monitoring. WSNs have many active research areas, including energy consumption, routing protocols, node deployment, localization, and security, making it a rich topic for research. However, node deployment still faces significant challenges, such as coverage ratio, connectivity, and overlapping sensor ranges. This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing node placement in WSNs using a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (mPSO) algorithm. Our method addresses the issues of coverage holes and overlapping sensor ranges. Initially, sensor nodes are randomly deployed within the region of interest (ROI). The mPSO algorithm iteratively refines the node positions to maximize area coverage while minimizing overlap, identifying gaps in the ROI and covering them with the nearest mobile node. This optimization process enhances sensor network coverage by over 35% compared to random deployment, improving overall performance and extending network lifetime.

articleTitle: Exploring Transfer Learning Techniques for Brain Tumor Diagnosis in MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized computer-aided diagnosis, improving image analysis, segmentation, detection, and classification. By accurately identifying and classifying abnormalities in X-rays, MRI, and CT scans, it can develop personalized treatment plans. However, building deep learning models requires a significant investment of time, money, and large datasets. This paper aims to establish a deep learning framework that can identify brain lesions using transfer learning techniques. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is still effective, but the diagnosis of malignant brain tumors remains challenging due to the complex structure of the brain. Using four architectures VGG16, VGG19, Xception, and DenseNet121 for brain tumor diagnosis, the effectiveness of deep transfer learning architectures was evaluated. With a batch size of 32, the following models are trained for 50 epochs. VGG16 had an accuracy of 97.6% on training data and 94% on validation data, VGG19 had an accuracy of 96.5% on training data and 89.2% on validation data, and Dense121 Net showed an accuracy of 100% on training data and 94% on validation data. In comparison, Xception showed an accuracy of 94.3% on validation data and 100% on the training set. The accuracy on test data for VGG16, VGG19, Xception, and DenseNet121 was 93.4%, 92.1%, 93.4%, and 94.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Binary and Multi Classification Model on Tax Evasion: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In this paper, a model was built to compare the performance of the following machine learning (ML) models: DT, RF, SVM, and MLP, using two types of classification: binary classification and multi classification. The researchers concluded that the MLP classifier was the most efficient using multi classifications, as the classifier gave an accuracy of 99.77%, a recall of 93.25%, a precision of 92.02%, and an F-score of 92.63%. Using the dataset provided by the Tax Authority of Yemen, which is related to the commercial and industrial profits tax explained in detail in other papers for the same authors, which consists of 1083 record, after the preprocessing of data. Keywords— ML techniques, RF, DT, SVM,MLP techniques, Binary classification, Multi-classification, Dataset of Tax.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Approach Using the Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Facial recognition technology has emerged as a pivotal tool in both security and technical domains. Its adoption has accelerated in several developed nations, where it finds applications across various sectors. For instance, institutions and businesses leverage this technology to monitor employees and detect unauthorized individuals, while banks utilize it to verify identities during cash withdrawals, serving as an alternative to traditional ATM cards. In this context, our research aims to propose a machine learning-based method for improving facial recognition accuracy. We conducted a thorough review of existing algorithms in the field and identified Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) as the most effective based on prior studies. To evaluate these algorithms, we compared SVM and PCA in the context of identity verification. Our experiments involved training the algorithms on a dataset comprising 5,749 facial images. The results demonstrated that the SVM algorithm significantly outperformed PCA in terms of accuracy. We believe that the successful application of the SVM algorithm can provide substantial benefits to institutions looking to enhance their security measures through reliable facial recognition systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Techniques for Chatbots Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Nowadays, advancements in technology have facilitated the development of machines that emulate human-like behavior. One notable application of this is conversational software agents which utilize natural language process (NLP) and artificial intelligence (AI), commonly referred to as Chatbots. These Chatbots serve various purposes and find application across diverse sectors such as business, healthcare, agriculture, and more. The evolution of Chatbots has been remarkable, prompting significant interest and research endeavours. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive survey of the techniques employed in enhancing Chatbot functionalities, offering a comparative analysis among them. Additionally, it delves into the nuances of these techniques, elucidating both their commonalities and distinctions. Through this exploration, the most commonly used algorithms in chatbots are reinforcement learning, BERT, NLP, and hybrid algorithms of artificial neural networks. The paper endeavours to identify research gaps that can guide future improvements in Chatbot technology, ultimately enhancing customer satisfaction levels.

articleTitle: Digital Signature Techniques for IoT Privacy and Trust Management
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In this article, a live solution for data acquisition from sensors and its representation on a web interface is discussed with the help of a Raspberry Pi in which MQTT is used for communication the Flask as the framework. Particularly emphasized is the improvement of the efficiency and the time needed for generating Digital signature using the ECDSA algorithm which is traditionally slow and requires much resources to be applied for real time IoT applications. For this, the authors try the approach of parallel processing on the Raspberry Pi which becomes many times shorter in generation of the signatures without any loss of the data integrity. It involves input data including temperature, humidity, motion, distance, and light intensity, processes them and then sends the input data over a secure MQTT connection. They also showed that the FCMP algorithm incurs less computation time, and the speed attained is almost constant and stable when parallel processing is incorporated in the generation of some of the ECDSA algorithm’s signatures. As presented in the experimental results, the processing time is reduced in comparison with sequential processing, which emphasizes the possibility of parallelization. Altogether we can state that the usage of Raspberry Pi and Flask as the core of the system along with MQTT as a communication protocol provides the necessary level of security and reliability for monitoring the sensor data in the IoT system. They show that parallel processing can indeed help enhance the cryptographic operations making this approach beneficial for performance optimization across multiple IoT applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Information Security Awareness Model to Advance Human Aspects in Humanitarian Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The digitalization and adoption of new technologies have become essential for humanitarian organizations, but they also expose them to cyber threats. To protect their systems and data, these organizations need to understand the security risks associated with advanced technologies. Information Security Awareness (ISA) has been recognized as a way to mitigate such risks, but existing models do not fully address the needs of humanitarian organizations. This research proposes an Enhanced Information Security Awareness model that includes additional focus areas of device securement and awareness of policy. Evaluating the model using the EHAIS-Q questionnaire shows that it positively influences information security awareness and improves the security culture within humanitarian organizations. In conclusion, the enhanced model fills the gap in addressing their specific needs and effectively enhances employees' understanding of information security practices.

articleTitle: An Intelligent System for Diagnosing Kidney Diseases Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Early diagnosis plays a critical role in preventing severe complications and fatalities associated with kidney disease, especially in regions like Saudi Arabia, where healthcare access may be limited. Prompt identification of the disease can significantly mitigate its severity and enhance patient outcomes. This study introduces an intelligent system for early kidney disease diagnosis utilizing machine learning (ML) models. We conducted a comparative analysis of various models, such as Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Gradient Boosting (GB), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), and Decision Tree (DT), with the SVC model achieving the highest accuracy of 72.00%. RF and KNN closely followed with 68.00% accuracy each, while the DT model, despite its interpretability benefits, achieved an accuracy of 56.00%. The interpretability of the DT model could be particularly advantageous in healthcare diagnostics where transparency is crucial. RF exhibited the highest precision at 0.71, proving effective in reducing false positives. The proposed system presents a promising solution for improving early kidney disease diagnosis and could be seamlessly integrated into mobile platforms, offering practical real-world applications for healthcare professionals and patients, especially in underserved areas.

articleTitle: A survey on graph-based methods for Software Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: In computer security, finding software vulnerabilities is essential since they provide serious security hazards to both individuals and companies. Known vulnerability variations or recently undiscovered vulnerabilities are frequently difficult to find using traditional vulnerability detection techniques. Graph representations are useful and successful methods for finding software system vulnerabilities. Conventional techniques for detecting vulnerabilities frequently depend on pattern matching and structural analysis, which may not be sufficient to find intricate and dynamic vulnerabilities. Graph-based methods, on the other hand, offer a more thorough and adaptable representation that catches the complex interrelationships and dependencies between code pieces. This research aims to make progress in the field of vulnerability detection by exploring the potential of graph-based techniques to address existing challenges and limitations: handling large-scale graphs can be computationally expensive, and detecting zero-day vulnerabilities remains a challenging task. By investigating how graph representations can effectively manage code diversity, capture intricate relationships, and improve vulnerability identification, we contribute to developing more robust and adaptive security mechanisms. Our comprehensive survey provides a thorough overview of graph-based vulnerability detection methods, offering insights into their potential, limitations, and effectiveness. This research serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners, guiding them in selecting appropriate methods and motivating further developments in this domain.

articleTitle: Design of IoT Electrical Freight Train Powered with Solar Energy for Sudanese Transport Market
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Over the past years transport facilities have developed into one of the most popular and actively exploring areas, due to the existing plans to improve the transportation systems between cities. Freight transport by rail is being seen as the next big growth point internationally. Consequently, for the development of this sector, reference should be made to the peculiarities of location, the volumes of trade turnover, as well as infrastructural investments. land transportation by use of trucks in Sudan are however experiencing some few hurdles such as; Fuel unavailable, costly, poorly provided, and nose-diving on the social face of our environment. This paper introduces a solution: a freight electric train powered by solar energy. Designed for fast, safe, and cost-effective goods delivery, the train is fully electronic, with real-time remote control via an Arduino microcontroller connected to an IoT cloud and equipped with sensors for efficiency and security. The paper details the design and performance evaluation of the system through experimental tests under various operating conditions. As presented by the results, it is possible to fully automate the electric train in real-time with a high accuracy of decision making to ensure safe and proper utilization of solar energy for better efficiency and sustainability in the railway’s freight transport logistics. The solar system productivity reached 6 V at midday, while the time to reach the destination was up to 17 sec when the train weight was 2.5 kg.

articleTitle: Environment-Aware 3D Mobility Simulation for the 5G and 6G Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: This paper addresses a significant challenge for future wireless networks, particularly those assisted by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and multi-access edge computing (MEC), which is the impact of 3D mobility in urban environments. Existing mobility models cannot facilitate 3D urban movement owing to control, collision avoidance, and awareness of the three-dimensional urban environment. Panda5gSim, is an open-source simulation framework, models 3D-controlled mobility in synthetic urban settings using a gaming engine. We presented a proof-of-concept, environment-dependent SINR (Signal-to-Interference plus noise), throughput, spectrum efficiency, and handover rate model for omnidirectional and 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) directional antennas. These results serve as benchmarks for this methodology. Furthermore, Panda5gSim can collect realistic transformations of objects and ray-tracing line-of-sight, rendering; it is precise and economic which make it a good alternative to the tracing-based mobility method, particularly at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: Traffic Localization in Smart Cities Using Internet of Crowd Sourcing
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: This paper aims to examine how IoT localization technologies have impacted on the smart city traffic application including Internet Vehicles (IoV), Internet of Crowed Sourcing (IoCS), Internet of Mobility (IoM), and the Internet of Artificial Intelligence (IoAI). IoV improves car to car and car to infrastructure interfaces by increasing traffic flow and reducing or eliminating risks. IoAI employs big data and machine learning technology to accurately capture traffic information and to timely signal appropriate traffic lights for better and safe navigation of self-driven cars. IoCS extending it to Crowdsourcing infrastructure to real-time data systems to improve traffic control and safety of pedestrians. IoM develops a single unified network of transportation opportunities incorporating both mass transit and personal vehicle modes, as well as micro-mobility solutions. Potential issues like data protection, integration, and system extensibility are also discussed throughout the paper, together with potential advancements in autonomous vehicles and artificial intelligence traffic management. Lastly, the research discusses the prospects of IoT localization for Smart City transportation developments. These systems integrating services like sensors, GPS, RFID and AI based models provide real time navigation, thus resulting in efficient traffic control and enhancing the prospects of developing sustainable urban environments.

articleTitle: Image-Based IoT Malware Detection Method Using Deep CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The widespread deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in various fields, such as agriculture and healthcare, has generated a vast amount of data, hence increasing the risk of data breaches. On the other hand, the demand for low-cost and easy-to-use smart products made them vulnerable to malware attacks, which aim to compromise or exploit IoT devices, resulting in damage and data loss. It has increased the necessity for effective and resilient strategies to safeguard these devices from malware threats. The study examines the feasibility of identifying IoT malware with several pre-trained deep convolutional neural network (CNN) models, such as AlexNet, VGG-16, VGG-19, InceptionV3, and MobileNet. The objective of this study is to employ various deep learning models to distinguish between malicious and benign images effectively. This study introduces a relatively new strategy that employs the chi-square goodness-of-fit method on an image dataset prior to model training, aiming to enhance performance and reduce the dataset size since it is noteworthy that this approach is not typically used directly on images. The suggested system's performance has been assessed using the IOT_Malware dataset based on standard performance metrics. The findings of this study indicate that VGG-19 and VGG-16 achieved the highest accuracy among the other models, with scores of 99.09% and 98.55%, respectively, demonstrating their perfect ability to produce the most accurate predictions, followed by MobileNet, InceptionV3, and AlexNet, which attained accuracies of 98.10%, 98.01%, and 97.65%, respectively. Moreover, this research paper presents a state-of-the-art evaluation to add to the system's reliability.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Anonymization Systems Against Website Fingerprinting Attacks Using Machine Learning Algorithms: Implementation and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Website Fingerprinting (WF) is a statistical traffic analysis attack, that allows a local, passive eavesdropper to determine a client’s web activity by leveraging features from her packet sequence. These attacks break the privacy expected by users of Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs). The basic idea of this kind of attack is to derive a website’s fingerprints from traffic and observed patterns, which can be followed when a website is visited. A library of website fingerprints is created for many interesting websites. This library of previously recorded fingerprints is then compared with the traffic patterns, which could be observed if some anonymization service is used. This lets the attacker learn which websites are downloaded, even if all traffic is encrypted. In this paper, the attack was implemented against the offered protection by a specific anonymization system to reproduce the results reported in the literature. We achieved over 94% accuracy when applied on a new set of monitored sites. Finally, a new suggested costeffective countermeasure was proposed, reducing the success of those attacks to less than 50%.

articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities in Healthcare and Industrial IoT: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has changed many industries by enabling smart devices to transmit data, operate autonomously, and interact in real-time. Among its most prominent applications are in healthcare and industrial sectors, where IoT is classified into two classes: massive Machine-Type Communication (mMTC) and Ultra-Reliable Low Latency Communication (URLLC). While mMTC devices prioritize low energy consumption and can handle large-scale deployments with minimal data rates, URLLC devices are focused on mission-critical applications requiring ultra-low latency and high reliability. This paper examines the challenges and opportunities of IoT implementation in healthcare and industrial sectors, focusing on interoperability, data security, and scalability issues. The objective is to provide actionable solutions for the effective integration of IoT technologies. The investigation shows that in healthcare, mMTC is utilized for non-critical monitoring, while URLLC supports critical tasks like remote surgery. In industrial settings, mMTC improves processes like supply chain management, while URLLC enables automation and real-time control of machinery. Despite these opportunities, challenges such as data privacy, security, interoperability, and reliability remain. Addressing these issues is crucial for unlocking the full potential of IoT in healthcare and industrial sectors.

articleTitle: A Performance Scoring Approach for QoS Optimization in Private 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Performance benchmarking is crucial for optimizing networks, including 5G Non-Public Networks (5G-NPN). Since one of the major advantages of 5G-NPN is to guarantee Quality of Service (QoS), ensuring optimal performance for their diverse applications is critical. This requires adjustments and testing of various radio-related parameters. Also, performance analysis and benchmarking need to be done based on the evaluation of relevant Key Parameter Indicators (KPIs) in order to identify the parameter set for the optimum performance for each application’s requirements. Many published results on performance benchmarking often lack transparency in their scoring methods. Additionally, QoS benchmarking evaluation for 5G-NPN use cases needs further steps due to the varying ranges of their KPIs. For example Block Error Rate (BLER) is mostly represented by percentage, while Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) and Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) are negative values.3GPP in TR 103.559 outlines practices for benchmarking network QoS, with a focus on Speech and multimedia Transmission Quality (STQ). This paper extends these outlines to evaluate 5G-NPN performance by defining a multi-objective function. We select a specific 5G-NPN use case as an example and apply four tests with varying network configurations. After each test, we collect most relevant 5G KPIs. To facilitate comparison, all KPIs are rescaled to a common scale. Additionally, we assign weights to each KPI based on its significance in the chosen use case. By combining rescaling and weight assignments, we propose a single metric that effectively characterizes the overall network performance for 5G-NPNs based on their specific use case requirements.

articleTitle: IoMT Availability Threats Attacks and Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Healthcare professionals may monitor and treat patients more effectively with IoT, which improves patient outcomes. However, there are also a lot of risks associated with this connection, especially provisioning attacks, which take advantage of holes in devices' network connections. This study examines the medical risks connected to availability assaults in Internet of Things systems, reviewing existing research on mitigating these risks. This article aims to review the literature that studies the availability in the IoT network and the threats it faces at both the level of data availability or availability in the system and the proposed solutions against attacks, where attacks were studied based on the targeted technologies once and based on the layers that were worked on again. It is noted that the dominant feature in this field is the use of attack detection systems and their integration with AI algorithms for different purposes such as classifying attacks and supporting systems while enhancing and deepening system properties such as privacy and transparency to increase trust in the IoT environment in general.

articleTitle: Assessment of IT Governance Maturity Level for Yemeni Telecom Sector Using COBIT 2019 Framewor006B
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Information technology (IT) plays a crucial role in business operations most organizations rely on IT resources for gaining competitive advantages and creating innovative and continuous values. This increased the importance of enterprise IT governance (EGIT) and developed the recent version of the control objectives for information and related technology (COBIT), COBIT 2019 framework. It identifies the seven components of an effective EGIT system: processes, organizational structures, information flows and items, people, skills and competencies, policies and procedures, culture, ethics and behavior, services, infrastructure, and applications. The EGIT maturity level (ITGML) assessment helps to align the EGIT with strategic objectives. This study aims to assess the ITGML of the Yemeni telecom sector using COBIT 2019 framework. A quantitative method was applied, with a 73.6% response rate (148 out of 201 questionnaires collected). The study revealed that the current ITGML is 3.48, reflecting a defined maturity level. The findings suggested that IT governance practices based on COBIT 2019 are well documented and standardized within the Yemeni telecom sector.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Blockchain for Detection and Prevention Abuse of Privileges
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Privilege abuse within organizations is a major concern because it can lead to security breaches caused by malicious actions or behavior from employees. It is one of the key sources of insider threats in organizational systems. This paper presents an integrated approach to detecting and preventing privilege abuse by employees, focusing on identifying malicious activities. This is achieved by combining artificial intelligence and blockchain technology. RNN is used to analyze malicious behavior, while blockchain ensures a secure, decentralized ledger to prevent abuse. The goal is to combine the RNN model with blockchain technology to detect and prevent privilege abuse. The LSTM model was implemented as an API to identify any malicious activity by employees, and the classification results were stored on the blockchain to ensure security, trust, and data integrity. Experiments using the CERT r4.2 dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a classification accuracy of 98.75% with low false positives and false negatives in detecting insider threats.

articleTitle: Wireless Fine Time Measurement Implementation and Analysis in Indoor Factory Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Positioning and accurate time delay measurement techniques have been used with the Internet of Things (IoT) and embedded systems due to their importance in providing location information for the communicating nodes. In the last two decades, positioning techniques were introduced using the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) of Wi-Fi signals and time-based techniques. Fine Timing Measurement (FTM) is the most important time-based technique, which relies on the captured timestamps during the messaging between nodes. Thus, in addition to its originally intended application for wireless localization, it can be used for the future of Wi-Fi Time Sensitive Networking (WTSN), where low latency, low jitter, and precise time synchronization play an important role in Industrial IoT (IIOT)-oriented applications.The presented work considers FTM’s behavior and performance measurements, especially in a factory environment with different room sizes. An Automated Physical Test Bed (APTB) and emulated multipath propagation model based on ITU-R radio wave propagation standard for the factory environment are considered in the work. The results show that the FTM performance is noticeably affected by multipath signal propagation, thus increasing RTT, delay, and fluctuation in jitter and resulting in a noticeable degradation in RSSI. In contrast, the total number of correctly received frames is not affected, indicating the efficiency and reliability of the Wi-Fi FTM technique.

articleTitle: Efficient Deep Post-Decision State Learning for Privacy-Conscious Offloading in MEC-Enabled 6G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: With the growing demand for data-intensive applications, offloading tasks to multi-access edge computing (MEC) servers has become essential. However, privacy concerns arise as sensitive data is transmitted to remote servers. To address this, the proposed method uses deep learning techniques to intelligently analyze and classify data packets, ensuring that only non-sensitive information is offloaded. This paper proposes a novel approach called a deep post-decision state (PDS) learning privacy-concerned offloading in MEC-enabled 6G Environments. A Post-Decision State (PDS) approach that selectively selects data packets while maintaining privacy is used to train the deep learning model. The suggested method successfully balances the trade-off between increasing system performance and safeguarding user privacy to achieve privacy-aware offloading in MEC-enabled 6G networks, as shown by the experimental findings. Also, it performs noticeably better than the traditional DQN, according to simulation data.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Framework for High-Precision Image Reconstruction in Complex Scattering Media
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Imaging in complex scattering media, such as fog or turbid environments, presents significant challenges due to random light scattering, which distorts images and obscures object details. Traditional techniques have struggled to produce high-quality reconstructions, especially when dealing with optically thick or dynamic scattering media. In this paper, we present a powerful deep-learning-based framework that includes an optical system designed to generate severely degraded speckle patterns. To address this, we fine-tuned a U -Net architecture to recover original images from highly distorted speckle patterns. Our approach uses multi-scale feature extraction and Mean Squared Error (MSE) as a loss function, to improve structural detail and overall image quality. Comprehensive evaluations were performed using a variety of metrics, including the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), demonstrating that the proposed model consistently outperforms existing methods, including GAN-based approaches, in reconstructing extensively scattered images. Quantitative results reveal that our model has an SSIM of 0.91 and a PSNR of 23.67, which are much higher than those produced by competing models. Qualitative comparisons support the greater reconstruction of small details and finer edges.

articleTitle: Review of Techniques Used in Computer-Aided Detection and Diagnosis for Breast Cancer Using Mammograms
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Breast Cancer (BC) is one of the most common and threatening diseases within the female population. The early and accurate diagnosis of diseases is crucial in increasing the lives of patients and their survival. The group of vulnerable people has been realized, especially women, who are at high risk of breast cancer. This review discusses the methods used in computer-aided detection and diagnosis of breast cancer using mammograms, the advantages and disadvantages of these methods, and recent improvements and developments by analyzing the secondary resources. This work examines article papers that have documented the application of the techniques and were published between the years, 2015 (the earliest publications dealing with breast cancer detection) and 2024.

articleTitle: Adaptive Translation of English to Arabic Movie Subtitles Using GPT-3.5 Turbo and FAISS
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: This research explores adaptive machine translation, focusing on the translation of English-to-Arabic movie subtitles using advanced large language models such as GPT-3.5 Turbo. Utilizing Sentence-Transformer to generate embeddings and FAISS for efficient retrieval enhances the translation quality, particularly in preserving idiomatic expressions and contextual nuances. The evaluation metrics—BLEU, CHRF, and TER—show significant improvements, with BLEU increasing by up to 12% over baseline systems. These results underscore the potential of adaptive techniques for enhancing subtitle translations in real-time, especially for complex languages like Arabic. The findings point towards the future development of more effective, domain-specific translation applications.

articleTitle: Coordinated Formation Control for Swarm Flying Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Swarm robotics has gained a lot of interest because of its potential for effective group behavior across various fields. This paper presents an in-depth study on Coordinated Formation Control (CFC) for Swarm Flying Robots (SFRs), focusing on developing a reliable CFC algorithm to handle the challenges in coordinating a group of flying robots. The goal is to form specific shapes and perform shape transitions as a team. The research addresses the swarm formation control problem, which involves having the robots move, work together, and arrange themselves in the intended formation, then maintain that formation while in motion. The approach uses a method based on linear assignments to establish the positions of the robots relative to one another and includes a pattern vector to represent these positions. A weighted confidence matrix is used to show how much information is being shared between the robots. We tested the CFC algorithm’s performance through simulations, considering typical conditions as well as challenging situations with potential robot failures. The results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve and maintain complex formations even when adapting to changing environments or facing failures. The study also explores different failure scenarios and suggests ways to minimize their effect on the swarm’s behavior. This work helps move the field of swarm robotics forward by offering insights into effective strategies for managing CFC in SFRs.

articleTitle: Impact of Integrating Lean, Agile, and DevOps with ITIL4 Framework for Modern IT Service Management
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: During the global pandemic, the phenomenon of digital transformation has turned into a necessity for organizations to facilitate either service delivery or operational efficiency. A big part of this attempt is ITIL v4, which is a holistic framework in IT service management. It helps you to link IT methodologies with business objectives as a whole.This allows them to follow an end-to-end service value framework to manage the full life cycle of services: strategy, design, deployment, and continual improvement. This framework is flexible and collaborative, and it fits well into more advanced technology, which may be utilized within the boundaries of automation, AI, etc., making modern service management possible.How is ITIL4 inspired by the Lean principles and brings an Agile/DevOps way of working into alignment to follow within enterprises to address the speed at which digital transformation happens? This integration will bake these practices into your stock ITSM. Organizations will be much better placed to adapt to new customer demands, speed up service delivery, and improve continuously.In this article, we explain how ITIL4 practices and elements can work with Lean and Agile/DevOps principles to provide readers with a solid understanding of the combined frameworks that help fuel digital transformation.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Quantum Internet on Telemedicine Technology: Enhancing Healthcare Delivery, Speed, and Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The development of telemedicine technology indicates a shift in access to healthcare services and patients’ desire for more convenient healthcare makes it a key tool in healthcare delivery. However, the process of transmitting and processing data with a high level of speed, security, privacy, performance, and reliability is an issue of utmost importance. Recently, researchers have focused on the quantum internet, which represents the pinnacle of technological progress, opens up new horizons and forms a fundamental pillar in improving the quality of healthcare services and providing healthcare constantly. This research aims to explore the impact of the quantum internet on the functions, processes, and applications of telemedicine technology. The importance of this topic is to reshape the ways of interaction with healthcare. By exploring this impact, the improvements brought by integrating of quantum internet with telemedicine technologies are highlighted to ensure the speed of transmission, processing, security of medical information, and data exchange. The results show the quantum internet improves processes, functions, and applications of telemedicine technology to provide medical services at quantum speed. Finally, the authors discuss the integration challenges of quantum internet with telemedicine technology to provide researchers with a wide area of research.

articleTitle: Static Arabic Sign Language Recognition in Real Time Using Machine Learning and MediaPipe
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Sign language is a form of visual communication used by individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing to communicate. This visual language relies on gestures, handshapes, facial expressions, and body movements to convey meaning rather than spoken words. Therefore, to improve the lives of deaf or hard of hearing people in the Arab community, a more comfortable approach to learning and working must be developed. This paper presents an interactive computer vision-based system for recognizing static hand gestures (letters and numbers) in Arabic sign language in real-time. The MediaPipe framework is used to extract features (hand landmarks) from each image, and a support vector machine to recognize the static gesture inputted in front of the camera and then translate it into its equivalent text and voice, an approach developed to bridge the communication gap between deaf and hearing people. Experiments were conducted using HopeArSL, a large dataset that collected 12,000 images of 40 Arabic sign language gestures. This approach's experiments showed 100% and 99.94% training accuracy for numbers and alphabet letters, respectively. The accuracy and average response time in real-time for numbers and alphabet letters were (98.08%, 1.43 ms) and (99.09%, 7.48 ms), respectively.

articleTitle: A New Architecture for Decentralized Cybersecurity Mesh (DCSM) Using Blockchain Technology for Distributed Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Cybersecurity Mesh Architecture (CSMA) is a promising new approach to cybersecurity that has the potential to improve network and information security. As networks become more complex and widespread, detecting and responding to threats has become more difficult. It has also led to security creep that leads to complexity of management, fragmentation of visibility, and limits organizations ability to respond effectively to threats. These and similar challenges have made integration with CSMA a necessity for today's organizations. The cybersecurity mesh can be viewed as centralizing security management and distributing the application of this management, but in some completely distributed networks, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, Edge Computing, Big Data, etc., the cybersecurity mesh is not compatible with them because it applies the principle of central management. Therefore, the researchers propose, in this paper, to change the cybersecurity mesh architecture. The cybersecurity mesh will be completely distributed using blockchain technology, where the network security infrastructure will first be changed to the blockchain network. After that, blockchain technology will be integrated into each layer of the proposed cybersecurity mesh. Finally, the proposed architecture will be evaluated by ensuring complete distribution and the expected security provided by the cybersecurity mesh.

articleTitle: Synchronous Task Allocation and Trajectory Optimization for Autonomous Drone Swarm
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: As applications become increasingly complex, robust solutions are needed for coordinating drone swarms to perform tasks autonomously. Efficient task assignment and trajectory planning are essential for optimizing the coordination and performance of swarm flying robots across various scenarios. This paper proposes a strategy to simultaneously address allocation and path planning problems for swarm flying robots, with the aim of optimally and efficiently assigning tasks and planning paths for multiple drones. Leveraging coordination and local interactions among drones, the algorithm optimally assigns tasks to individual drones and generates collision-free trajectories for each member. Through extensive simulation evaluations, this work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in achieving optimal trajectories while ensuring dynamic feasibility and inter-drone collision avoidance. The results highlight the algorithm’s potential to enhance the coordination and performance of swarm flying robots in various real-world applications, providing a versatile solution to address task allocation and path planning challenges.

articleTitle: Anomaly-Based Intrusion Detection System in WSN using DNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are a necessary principle in WSN security, which can successfully prevent various hackers' and intruders' attempts to hack the network. In this research, we address the problem of achieving high accuracy in detecting intrusions in WSNs due to specific characteristics of WSN data, including the appropriate dataset, the drawbacks of feature selection, and choosing the proper algorithms for the classification process. In this paper, we proposed the anomaly-based IDS model using the DNN algorithm and mutual information (MI) technology to select features. The proposed model has been implemented using the Python language used in the Anaconda platform and relying on the standard NSL-KDD dataset. The experimental results showed the capability of the proposed model to achieve high-performance accuracy in intrusion detection using the DNN algorithm compared to the state-of-the-art. The proposed model outperforms other previous relevant works by 3.65% enhancement in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on Automotive Hacking
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Using cutting-edge technologies in automobiles has increased concerns about car hacking. Network connections like Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and 4G LTE have expanded the attack surface. The weaknesses in hardware and software may allow unauthorized access to private systems, endangering drivers and passengers. Hackers exploit the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus to manipulate car functionality, potentially causing accidents. Vehicle manufacturers and cybersecurity experts are implementing stronger security measures to mitigate this threat. Comprehensive security risk assessments are conducted throughout a vehicle’s lifespan, involving identifying assets, monitoring security threats, and analyzing concerns. Car hacking highlights the need for modern cybersecurity safeguards. This paper briefly overviews the rise in cyber threats against smart technologies, such as attacks connected to smart vehicles. It discusses major developments in connected and autonomous car technology, the challenges posed by growing cyber threats, and how important automotive cybersecurity and IT are to preserving these breakthroughs.

articleTitle: Navigating Energy: Unveiling Power Consumption Patterns in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Energy consumption is critical in self-driving cars and is set to change how transportation works. In this paper, we address the challenges of vehicle energy consumption by examining how the location of self-driving cars affects their energy use over time, looking at two-and three-dimensional aspects. Using models and real-world data, we examine the energy usage patterns of vehicle systems within MATLAB to reveal insights into their design and operation. In this paper, the power dynamics of cars that significantly contribute to the discussions of practical and sustainable self-driving transportation are introduced. The main goal is to demonstrate how power management may be revolutionized for self-driving car systems, ensuring maximum performance and dependability in today’s dynamic mobility scene. The findings show that enhancing autonomous vehicles’ design and operational strategies ensures their reliability and optimizes performance in today’s rapidly evolving transportation landscape.

articleTitle: Predicting Customer Churn in Telecommunication Companies in Somalia using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: With the use of machine learning techniques, this paper offers a thorough method for forecasting customer attrition in Mogadishu, Somalia's telecom industry. The rapidity at which consumers stop using a telecom provider is known as customer churn, and it presents a serious financial risk. The objective of this project is to improve prediction accuracy and provide guidance for targeted client retention efforts by utilizing a range of machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, Decision Trees, and Logistic Regression. The study utilizes a strong approach that includes feature selection, data preparation, and model assessment in order to successfully handle the subtleties of client behavior patterns. The results show that Random Forest models outperform other models in anticipating possible customer attrition, which makes proactive client retention initiatives possible. This study contributes to both practical applications and the theoretical understanding of customer behavior in high-churn environments.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study of Prominent International University Ranking Systems: Exploring the Potential of Yemeni Universities for Rankings
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Specifically targeting Yemeni universities, the focus lies on their potential to enter these rankings and enhance their positions such as Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) World University Ranking (QS), Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), Webometrics Ranking, Times Higher Education (THE) World University Ranking, and SCImago Institutions (SIR) Rankings. Its objective is to encourage Yemeni universities to prioritize the criteria outlined in these rankings and view them as a means to access other international rankings. The research tackles the challenge of comprehending the criteria and application process required for Yemeni universities to participate in these rankings, as well as the rankings they have achieved. The study underscores the importance of this research by providing Yemeni university administrators with valuable insights into the criteria used for international rankings and the rankings obtained by Yemeni universities. This understanding can facilitate efforts to enhance the quality of higher education within these institutions. The findings of the study reveal that there are two Yemeni universities listed in the QS. The University of Science and Technology, ranks 151-170, while Thamar University, ranks 171-200 for 2023. While in 2024, the University of Science and Technology ranked first locally and the University of Aden ranked second. This paper investigates the participation of Yemeni universities in global ranking systems such as ARWU, THE, QS, and SIR, with the aim of enhancing their international standing. It highlights the challenges and opportunities for Yemeni universities to meet ranking criteria, offering insights that can help improve the quality of higher education.

articleTitle: The Influence of Hyperparameters on GANs Performance for Medical Image Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have accomplished compelling performance in many fields such as image-to-image transformation, image data generation, translation of image information into text information, and many more. In GANs, two neural networks, a generator and discriminator, compete with each other in an adversarial manner, and due to their robust generating ability, GANs can produce high-quality images for human reference. Thus, GANs are a very promising approach artificial intelligence field. In this work, GANs with optimized hyperparameters selection are proposed to generate skin lesion medical images that are indistinguishable from the real images and analyze the quality of generated images using image quality metrics including Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). Additionally, the impact of hyperparameters including learning rate, batch size, latent space size, and number of epochs is analyzed against GANs performance. The experimental results indicate that the learning rate is the most effective hyperparameter for GAN stability and performance. Moreover, latent dimension, batch size, and number of epochs have a relatively small impact when paired with an appropriate learning rate thus good learning rate provides flexibility in optimizing these hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Identifying Tajweed Rules: A Case Study on Noon Saakin and Tanween
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: This study focuses on the classification of Tajweed rules from audio data and evaluates the effectiveness of various machine learning (ML) algorithms in emotion classification from speech. The dataset was created using audio samples, with a special focus on the Tajweed rules of Noon Saakinah and Tanween. The dataset exhibited class imbalance, and various data augmentation (DA) techniques were employed to address this. Preprocessing involved silence removal, normalization, and noise reduction to enhance the data's quality. Comprehensive feature extraction, covering both time-domain and frequency-domain features, was performed to capture the audio's key characteristics. Several ML models, including Random Forest (RF), support vector machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), were applied, and their performance was evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The RF model achieved the highest accuracy (0.8222), outperforming other models such as MLP (0.7905) and Gradient Boosting (GB) (0.7746). Traditional models such as Naive Bayes (NB) and Logistic Regression (LR) exhibited lower performance, highlighting the limitations of simpler methods in complex classification tasks.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Energy-Saving Algorithm for Narrowband Internet of Thing’s Indoor Localization Based on Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: The narrowband Internet of Things’ (NB-IoT) algorithm must be streamlined to manage service quality and maximize network performance as the number of devices continuous to grow. In this paper, we proposed a convex optimization model for distributing multiple sources using the Karun-Kush-Tucker (KKT) conditions in networks with a single energy-harvesting (EH) relay. As NB-IoT devices proliferate, co-channel interference increases, challenging the performance enhancements that non-orthogonal multiple access (NMA) aims to deliver. To address this, we rigorously tested our proposed approach, demonstrating its effectiveness. The results show a 31.93% increase in energy efficiency, a 7.23% improvement in data rate proportional fairness, and a 36.76% boost in spectrum efficiency. Our approach significantly improves network metrics by strategically organizing resources.

articleTitle: Secure Authentication in Smart Home Environment Using SGX and Biometrics: Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
abstract: Recently, our lifestyles have evolved to be smarter, with various devices becoming available for daily activities, such as smartphones, smart watches, smart lighting, and smart cameras. A smart home, also known as a connected home, uses smart internet-connected devices that enable remote monitoring and administration of appliances and systems. This study aims to analyze the environment of smart homes, focusing on the authentication processes that secure these systems. It explores modern technologies supporting authentication, such as Intel software guard extensions (SGX) and biometrics systems. SGX utilizes isolation techniques to protect data in secure enclaves, while biometrics measure people's unique physical and behavioral characteristics. These technologies are used to build many layers of defense to protect homeowners' privacy. Moreover, the Internet of Things (IoT) is crucial in enhancing smart home functionalities. This study also examines the implementation of IoT in smart homes and the ways they are utilized and communicated. Additionally, it discusses the lessons learned and identifies current challenges in this evolving environment.

articleTitle: Firefly Algorithm Based Proportional Integral Derivative Controller for AQM in TCP Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 1st International Conference on Emerging Technologies for Dependable Internet of Things (ICETI)
